How this works
  • Every dot is one walk, one conversation, one person. All 62 documented walks took place at different times, on different days, and at different times of year. But for this visualization, the walks are layered, sharing space and time.
  • Click any dot on the map, or any name in the list, to open that walk.
  • The selected walk comes to the front in gold; the rest dim so you can follow it clearly.
  • Its panel holds a Postwalk Reflection, and a One Week Follow-Up below it when one was recorded.
  • The map stays interactive: pan and zoom freely, even with a walk open.
  • Speed controls how fast the walks replay. 1× is the true pace they were walked at.

You are invited to explore this map and the more than 60 walks I did with Studio Olafur Eliasson.

Each dot is one walk, one conversation, one person.

You can click on the dots moving on the map or select one from the list on the left.

You can read quotes from the anonymized post-walk reflections as well as my notes and one-week follow-ups.

This map is a repository for my research into walking as a creative practice, a way of connecting to ideas, with one another, and the living world around us.
